title: Cirta report, version 1
description: What `cirta inspect --json` prints: one entry per file. Version 1 is additive: new formats, finding kinds and note codes may appear within it, so a reader must accept values it does not know. A change that removes or renames a field is a new version, with a new schema tag.

file.description: The path as given on the command line.

error.description: Why the file was not inspected, in the report's language.

code.description: The refusal's code, when it has one: unsupported, unparseable, encrypted-pdf, empty-file…

result.description: Also what inspectFile() returns in the library.

format.description: pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, odt, ods, odp, doc, xls, ppt, msg, eml, ipynb, svg, html, markdown, jpeg, png, zip, text — more may come.

kind.description: identity, provenance, timestamp, environment, invisible-character, deceptive-link, active-content, deceptive-name — more may come.

location.description: Where the value lives: a part path, a field, 'member → field' inside an archive.

label.description: The field's name, in English; front-ends translate it.

value.description: What was found. Personal data found by --pii is masked.

affectsVerifiability.description: True when removing it changes how third parties verify the file (C2PA).

code.description: A caveat, as a code: scope:…, limit:…, removed:…, kept:… — front-ends word it.
